title: Factory... Oh Sweet Factory
statementMd:
**This problem has nothing to do with problem A**

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0c9a6812a867502369424aac49f078cae96f8d4f.png)

Danna is the owner of "Dulce Alfajor", a renowned traditional Argentine sweets company. Due to her immense success, her factory has expanded into a massive complex with strict safety protocols.

The factory layout can be modeled as a **directed acyclic graph** with $n + 1$ rooms and $m$ directed halls, numbered from $0$ to $n$. Room $0$ is the main entrance, while rooms $1$ through $n$ are covered in sticky candy and need to be cleaned.

Danna needs to assign a color preference $C_i$ to each room $i$ ($1 \le i \le n$) each room needs to have **one** asigned color. She will then hire exactly one worker for each **unique** color used. The cleaning process operates under the following rules:

- Room $0$ contains all colors, so any worker can start their cleaning route there.
- Each worker is assigned a specific color $c$ and will only enter and clean rooms assigned color $c$.
- A worker assigned color $C_w$ starts at room $0$ and traverses a directed path $0 \to v_1 \to v_2 \to \dots \to v_m$ where for every room ($1  \lt = j  \lt = m$) the color is the same as the color of the worker ($C_w = C_{v_j}$), cleaning every room along that path.
- Every room assigned color $c$ must be visited **at least once** and cleaned by that worker in a single route.
- Every room from $1$ to $n$ must be visited and cleaned by **exactly** one worker.
- Workers will always choose the path that **maximizes** the amount of rooms they can clean

It is guaranteed that there is a **direct corridor from Room $0$ to every room** $v \in [1, n]$, and no room $v \in [1, n]$ has a corridor leading to Room $0$.

Note that a worker can visit a room even if it has already been cleaned.

Help Danna determine the minimum number of unique colors $K$ required to clean the entire factory, and output a valid color assignment $C_1, C_2, \dots, C_n$ ($1 \le C_i \le K$) for rooms $1$ through $n$.

## Input

The first line contains two space-separated integers $n$ and $m$ ($1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$, $n \le m \le n + 2 \cdot 10^5$) — the number of candy-covered rooms (excluding room $0$) and the number of directed halls between rooms $0$ through $n$, respectively.

Each of the next $m$ lines contains two space-separated integers $u_i$ and $v_i$ ($0 \le u_i \le n$, $1 \le v_i \le n$, $u_i \neq v_i$), representing a directed hall from room $u_i$ to room $v_i$. It's guaranteed that there exist a directed hall from room 0 to every other room and there are no multiple edges.

## Output

On the first line, print a single integer $K$ ($1 \le K \le n$) — the minimum number of unique colors required to clean all rooms.

On the second line, print $n$ space-separated integers $C_1, C_2, \dots, C_n$ ($1 \le C_i \le K$), where $C_i$ represents the color assigned to room $i$.

If there are multiple valid color assignments using $K$ colors, you may print any of them.
statementZhMd:
**本题与 A 题无关**

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0c9a6812a867502369424aac49f078cae96f8d4f.png)

Danna 是著名的阿根廷传统糖果公司“Dulce Alfajor”的所有者。由于生意极为成功，她的工厂已扩建成一个规模庞大、实行严格安全规程的厂区。

工厂的布局可以建模为一张**有向无环图**，其中有 $n + 1$ 个房间和 $m$ 条有向走廊，房间编号从 $0$ 到 $n$。房间 $0$ 是主入口，而房间 $1$ 到 $n$ 都沾满了黏糊糊的糖果，需要清理。

Danna 需要为每个房间 $i$（$1 \le i \le n$）指定一种颜色 $C_i$，每个房间必须被指定**恰好一种**颜色。随后，她会为每种用到的**不同**颜色恰好雇用一名工人。清理过程遵循以下规则：

- 房间 $0$ 包含所有颜色，因此任何工人都可以从这里开始自己的清理路线。
- 每名工人被分配一种特定的颜色 $c$，并且只会进入和清理被指定为颜色 $c$ 的房间。
- 被分配颜色 $C_w$ 的工人从房间 $0$ 出发，沿一条有向路径 $0 \to v_1 \to v_2 \to \dots \to v_m$ 行进，其中每个房间（$1  \lt = j  \lt = m$）的颜色都与该工人的颜色相同（$C_w = C_{v_j}$），并清理路径上的每个房间。
- 所有被指定为颜色 $c$ 的房间，都必须由对应的工人在同一条路线中**至少访问一次**并清理。
- 从 $1$ 到 $n$ 的每个房间，都必须由**恰好**一名工人访问并清理。
- 工人总会选择能使自己清理的房间数量**最多**的路径。

保证**从房间 $0$ 到每个房间都有一条直达走廊**，其中 $v \in [1, n]$，且任何房间 $v \in [1, n]$ 都没有通向房间 $0$ 的走廊。

注意，即使一个房间已经被清理过，工人仍然可以访问它。

请帮助 Danna 求出清理整个工厂所需的最少不同颜色数 $K$，并输出房间 $1$ 到 $n$ 的一种合法颜色分配方案 $C_1, C_2, \dots, C_n$（$1 \le C_i \le K$）。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个以空格分隔的整数 $n$ 和 $m$（$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$，$n \le m \le n + 2 \cdot 10^5$）——分别表示沾满糖果的房间数量（不包括房间 $0$），以及房间 $0$ 到 $n$ 之间的有向走廊数量。

接下来 $m$ 行，每行包含两个以空格分隔的整数 $u_i$ 和 $v_i$（$0 \le u_i \le n$，$1 \le v_i \le n$，$u_i \neq v_i$），表示一条从房间 $u_i$ 通向房间 $v_i$ 的有向走廊。保证从房间 0 到其他每个房间都存在一条有向走廊，且图中没有重边。

## 输出格式

第一行输出一个整数 $K$（$1 \le K \le n$）——清理所有房间所需的最少不同颜色数。

第二行输出 $n$ 个以空格分隔的整数 $C_1, C_2, \dots, C_n$（$1 \le C_i \le K$），其中 $C_i$ 表示为房间 $i$ 指定的颜色。

如果存在多种使用 $K$ 种颜色的合法分配方案，你可以输出其中任意一种。
